record.text: The PM will supply five different front designs in a box.
The remote case should be hard plastic and transparent to enable backlighting.
The remote will not wake up; the power light doesn't work and it appears it may have been turned off.
Five interchangeable front panels will be provided in a box and used on the remote.
The cost is unclear; although a figure of twelve and a half euros per remote is mentioned, the total production cost remains undefined.
UI will provide UI's design to the group.
There is lack of information about the cost and viability of speech recognition, and discussions have been inconsistent.
ID will discuss the material options with PM.
The Real Reaction logo will be placed on the remote, and the fronts on the remote should be replaceable.
UI will paint prototype drawings on the smart board.
LED colors will be blue, red, and green; color cannot be chosen at purchase; color can be changed after purchase; there are multiple LEDs.
The remote will use rubber buttons for three-dimensional curved remotes; two-D curved design; wheel should be round; numbers at bottom; switch channel in the middle.
Skip the LCD option and use the second most expensive chip; use the regular chip; titanium will not be used.
The UI will follow up on the item discussed after this meeting.

gold.text: The Project Manager reviewed the minutes from the previous meeting.
The Marketing Expert gave a trendwatching report.
He found that a fancy look and feel was most important for users.
He also discussed the trend towards spongy materials.
The group discussed the cost of adding speech recognition, the LCD screen, and the advanced chip.
The User Interface Designer discussed the look of the interface with the group.
They discussed the placement and design of the buttons and decided to use scroll wheels for volume.
The Industrial Designer advised that flashy colors and rounded shapes be used.
The group discussed how to incorporate the logo and including changeable faces.
They discussed materials for the buttons and the backlight.
The group decided to use rechargeable batteries and a stand, to use plastic for the casing and buttons, and to not include an LCD screen.
The User Interface Designer and the Industrial Designer were instructed to draw the prototype at the next meeting, and the User Interface Designer was instructed to finalize the button placement.
The group finalized the look of the product, and eventually decided to incorporate speech recognition and an advanced chip.

The scroll wheel could be small and yellow, to match the Real Reaction colours.
The remote will include rechargeable batteries and will be used with a recharging stand.
The remote will feature plastic buttons and casing, rather than rubber.
The remote will not feature an LCD screen.
The remote will have rounded corners and be curved in two dimensions only, not in depth.
The group decided to design five changeable faces for the device.
They eventually decided to incorporate speech recognition and an advanced chip.
